title: Education
description: School seen from the inside: the uniform debate of an English girls' school and the five positions it produces - three for, one against, and one that holds both at once - with the words that carry it (a uniform, to distinguish, smart in the sense of tidy and well dressed, individuality, to suppress, to conform to, a community, an identity) and the language of stating and standing for an opinion; recognising an argumentative text from the openings of its paragraphs alone; the nine reflexive pronouns (myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, oneself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves), their spelling in -self and -selves, their place after the verb, why the pronoun you takes two of them, and the rule that a reflexive agrees with its own subject and not with the sentence before it; the examination room of lesson 19, seven pupils in trouble and the seven pieces of advice that answer them, including the pair that both speak of checking answers - one with no time left and one with time to spare; the words of examinations (to sit, to take, to pass, to fail, to cope with, to check, blank, to revise, revision) and the false friend that makes to pass mean to succeed; the six modal forms the exercise actually requires - had better, ought to and should for advice, needn't for what is not necessary and why it is not the negative of must, should have and shouldn't have for regret and for reproach about a past that cannot be repaired, and must for a conclusion drawn from evidence - plus will as an offer of help; and the last two steps of writing as a process, the first draft exchanged with a classmate and the final draft handed in
